claims: PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) (prospective — use of registry info in hiring); ICRAA §§1786.16, 1786.40 (prospective); FCRA §§1681b(b)(3), 1681d (prospective); UCL §17200 (prospective)
damages: Prospective. Offer of Temporary Employment (TaskUs, LLC, signed Sep. 14, 2026) states $22.00 per hour, non-exempt, San Jose delivery; anticipated assignment Sep. 23, 2026 through on or around Dec. 4, 2026; $1,000 retention bonus if still employed in good standing on Dec. 4. Statutory framework if the claim ripens: Penal Code §290.46(j)(4)(A) (actual or treble damages, $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages); ICRAA §§1786.50, 1786.52; FCRA §§1681n, 1681o; UCL restitution. No valuation until adverse action, if any.
defendants: TaskUs, LLC (prospective; offer-letter employer, 1650 Independence Drive, Ste 100, New Braunfels, TX 78132); TaskUs USA LLC (prospective; background-consent recipient); TaskUs Holdings, Inc. (NDA counterparty; named employer on the First Advantage saliva-drug-test order); TaskUs, Inc. (Mutual Arbitration Agreement counterparty). First Advantage is a prospective vendor defendant if a consumer/registry report from FA drives a non-hire (Matter 31 companion). Uber AV is the WorkDay campaign (R_2608_10812), not a named prospective defendant on this packet — the 2810.5 does not list Uber as the entity for whom the work is performed. DOES 1–10 for other hiring decision-makers if adverse action follows.

key_facts: On Sep. 14, 2026, TaskUs, LLC sent Brendan Ngwa Nforbi a signed Offer of Temporary Employment as a Teammate at $22.00 per hour (non-exempt), location USA - San Jose - San Jose (Delivery). Anticipated assignment Sep. 23, 2026 through on or around Dec. 4, 2026; $1,000 retention bonus if still employed in good standing on Dec. 4. Orientation Sep. 23–25 at 1631 N 1st Street, Suite 200, San Jose; production depot 3030 Corvin Dr., Santa Clara; closed-course training in Sonoma. The offer is at-will, contingent on job-related background screening and a Fair Chance Act process for conviction history, and says screening usually takes two weeks and employment may begin while screening is pending. The same day he signed the United States Background Consent Form (release of screening information to TaskUs USA LLC), the TaskUs Holdings, Inc. NDA/invention-assignment, and a Mutual Arbitration Agreement with TaskUs, Inc. whose covered claims include the background-check form or process. At 6:50 a.m. TaskUs emailed, from do_not_reply@fadv.com, 'You have been invited to start your background check' — Profile Advantage, powered by First Advantage (pa4.fadv.com; invite key GK5HGWELSS). That is the consumer-report track. The same CRA ran the FedEx (Matter 25) and UPS (Matter 26) employment screens; on information and belief the TaskUs report will be similar if not identical in format, including any NSOR / SOURCE OF RECORD: CALIFORNIA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY component if those items are on the TaskUs package. At 8:49 a.m. First Advantage separately ordered a Saliva Drug Test Full Service NonDOT for employer TaskUs Holdings, Inc. (Schedule ID 96558696; LabCorp-Milpitas in Walgreens; expires Sep. 17, 2026, 11:49 a.m. Eastern). Page 9 of the offer is the California medical-release for that drug/alcohol product. Do not collapse the drug screen into the background report. Same day, Profile Advantage opened Order WPS-361214148 (portal name Brendan Ngwanforbi). As of ~10:20 a.m. PDT: MVR, Federal Felony And Misdemeanor, PRICPGS, FADV National Criminal File, and Social Security Verification show Completed; Felony Including Misdemeanor and PRINSOS show In Progress. PRINSOS is First Advantage's national sex-offender search — the analogue of the UPS/FedEx NSOR line. The portal will not display the report until the order completes; a green check is not a result and is not a registry hit. No standalone ICRAA/FCRA disclosure is in this packet, and no adverse action has occurred. WorkDay requisition R_2608_10812 is 'Uber AV Teammate (SJ: 09/23/2026)' (candidate C261051599). Uber AV is the client campaign, not a defendant on this packet.
